title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Casual Loading, Super, and the Victorian Teacher Salary
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using 38 hours per week. Includes casual loading, super on top, and the Victorian teacher salary average from ABS data.
salarySummary: To estimate annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (assume 38) and then by 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full‑time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. When converting to annual pay, add the loading first. For example, a base rate of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with loading. Then multiply by 38 hours × 52 weeks to get an annual estimate of $65,342. Super is paid on the loaded amount.

faqs.q: How is super calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. It does not reduce your take‑home pay. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The super is not included in the annual salary figure shown in this conversion.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the simplest way to compare them is to convert one to the other. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This article assumes a 38‑hour week, which is the typical full‑time hours under the Fair Work system. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. The result is an estimate only – it does not include unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The Fair Work Act defines a full‑time week as 38 hours. Multiplying by 52 weeks gives a year‑round figure. For part‑time or casual workers, use your actual weekly hours. The fortnightly equivalent is simply weekly pay × 2. For example, a $30 per hour rate gives $1,140 per week (38 hours) and $2,280 per fortnight.

## Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Australia has a [National Minimum Wage](/topics/minimum-wage) set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Many employees are covered by awards that set higher minimum rates. For example, the **Victorian teacher salary** is typically governed by the Victorian Government Schools Agreement or the Independent Schools Award. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, Victoria’s full‑time ordinary time average weekly earnings were $2,041.10 in May 2026. That equates to an annual salary of about $106,137 (assuming 38 hours). This is an **average** for all full‑time workers in Victoria, not a median for any specific teaching role.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is therefore $33.05 per hour (including loading). When converting to annual pay, always apply the loading first. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator – the [timesheet](/) on this site has a checkbox to add 25% loading automatically.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer **on top** of your gross pay. It does not reduce your take‑home pay. For the 2026–27 year, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. If your annual gross exceeds that, super only applies up to that limit. For example, on a $100,000 salary, your employer contributes an extra $12,000 to your super fund. This is separate from your salary and is not included in the annual figure you see in a conversion.

For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare

Resident tax rates for 2026–27 are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The thresholds used here are the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 figures were not confirmed. This estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use the [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed breakdown.

## Putting It All Together: An Example

Suppose you are a casual worker earning the National Minimum Wage. Your base rate is $26.44 per hour. With 25% casual loading, your effective rate is $33.05. For a 38‑hour week:
- Weekly pay: $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
- Fortnightly pay: $1,255.90 × 2 = $2,511.80
- Annual gross: $1,255.90 × 52 = $65,306.80

Super at 12% adds $7,836.82 on top, but this goes to your super fund, not your pocket. Tax on $65,306.80 (using the 2026–27 scale) would be approximately $11,342 plus Medicare of $1,306, leaving an estimated take‑home of about $52,659 per year. Remember, this is an estimate.

## Award Rates and the Victorian Teacher Salary

Award rates often differ from the minimum wage. For teachers in Victoria, the relevant award or enterprise agreement sets minimum pay rates based on classification and experience. The ABS average of $2,041.10 per week for Victoria is a broad average across all full‑time occupations, not a median for teachers. If you are looking at a specific job offer, check the applicable award or agreement. Our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) can help you find the right rate.

## When to Use This Conversion

This conversion is useful for comparing a casual hourly offer with a permanent salary, or for budgeting. However, it does not account for:
- Unpaid overtime
- Penalty rates (e.g., weekends, nights)
- Allowances (e.g., travel, tools)
- Salary sacrifice arrangements

For a more precise calculation, especially if you have irregular hours, use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool and adjust the weekly hours.

## Summary

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours unless told otherwise)
- Casual loading of 25% is added to the base rate before conversion
- Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings, up to the contribution base
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take‑home pay
- The Victorian teacher salary average is $2,041.10 per week (full‑time ordinary time) – an average, not a median

Always check your specific award or agreement for the correct rate. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has the latest figures.
